verdict.rationale: Neon is real Postgres (not a lookalike), evidenced by connecting via standard psql/dbeaver clients, support for extensions like pgvector, and community confirmation it's genuinely Postgres under the hood (used by Vercel). However, Neon only supports Postgres — no MySQL or SQLite dialect compatibility is offered or claimed, and some architectural differences (storage/compute separation, S3-backed storage) draw community pushback on whether behavior fully matches traditional Postgres performance expectations. missing for 10: MySQL/SQLite dialect support, exhaustive extension-compatibility list, independent verification that all Postgres extensions/behaviors work identically at scale.
